newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SEOUL TO BAN BANKS FROM TAKING LOAN-TIED DEPOSITS.
newsitem.headline: SEOUL TO BAN BANKS FROM TAKING LOAN-TIED DEPOSITS.

text.p: South Korea's Office of Bank Supervision said on Tuesday it would ban banks from taking deposits as a precondition for small and medium-sized companies to get loans, effective August 18.
Such compensatory deposits have been common practice mainly due to limited loan resources compared to high demand.

The country's banking watchdog body also said in a statement all banks had to clear existing compensatory deposit accounts by September 13 either by offsetting deposits with loans or by calling off contracts.
The decision to have banks clear up existing compensatory deposits was aimed at keeping liquidity high ahead of the Chusok traditional Thanksgiving holidays, September 15-17, the statement said.
Most small and medium-sized companies usually experience hardships in getting loans to cover bonus payments ahead of Chusok, one of the country's biggest traditional holidays.
